fields.label: Species
fields.description: Select the organism from which the sample was obtained. Use the species-level taxonomy entry whenever possible; the submitted value should correspond to an NCBI Taxonomy term.

fields.label: Tissue
fields.description: Specify the tissue or anatomical structure from which the sample was collected. Select the most specific tissue term available from the Uberon for animals and PlantOntology for plants.

fields.label: Strain
fields.description: Enter the strain the organism if known. Use the designation commonly reported in publications or vendor documentation.

fields.label: Disease
fields.description: Specify any disease or pathological condition associated with the organism or sample source. Add multiple entries if more than one disease is relevant.

fields.label: Cellular Component
fields.description: Indicate the cellular location from which glycans or glycoproteins were isolated or are known to reside. Select the most appropriate Gene Ontology cellular component term.

fields.label: Developmental Stage
fields.description: Describe the developmental, growth, or life-cycle stage of the organism at the time of sampling. Use a clear and commonly accepted stage description.

fields.label: Other perturbation
fields.title: Were there external perturbations that might have an effect on the provided data?

fields.label: Radiation
fields.description: Describes exposure of the organism, tissue, or cells to ionizing or non-ionizing radiation prior to sample collection. Record the radiation source and dose when known.

fields.label: Chemical
fields.description: Describes exposure to a chemical substance that is not primarily administered as a therapeutic drug or nutrient. Include the chemical name and exposure conditions when available.

fields.label: Drug
fields.description: Describes treatment with a pharmaceutical, therapeutic, or experimental drug prior to sample collection. Include the drug name and dosage or concentration when available.

fields.label: Nutrient Modification
fields.description: Describes changes to nutrient availability, diet, or growth medium composition that may affect the biological system before sample collection. Include the modified nutrient when known.
fields.example: High-glucose medium (25 mM glucose), High Fat diet

fields.label: Environmental and Physical Conditions
fields.description: Describes exposure to environmental or physical conditions that induce a biological response prior to sample collection. Examples include changes in oxygen availability, temperature, or mechanical forces.

fields.label: Pathogen Exposure
fields.description: Describes exposure to or infection with a virus, bacterium, fungus, parasite, or other pathogen before sample collection. Include the pathogen name when known.

fields.label: Other
fields.description: Describes a perturbation that does not fit any of the predefined categories. Provide a clear description of the intervention.

fields.label: Tissue

fields.label: Cellular Component

fields.label: Developmental Stage
fields.description: Describe the developmental, growth, or life-cycle stage of the organism at the time of sampling. Use a clear and commonly accepted stage description.

fields.label: Variant
fields.description: Enter the name or identifier of the organism variant being studied. Use the designation reported in publications, stock centers, or laboratory records so the variant can be traced to its underlying genetic alterations.

fields.label: Cell line
fields.description: Select the cell line from Cellosaurus whenever available. If a modified or derivative cell line was used, choose the corresponding Cellosaurus entry or provide an approved 'other' value when necessary.

fields.label: Phenotype
fields.description: Describes an observable phenotype associated with the genetic alteration, protein mutation, or biological background. Phenotypes may be morphological, developmental, physiological, behavioral, cellular, molecular, or disease-related.

fields.label: Genetic Background Alteration
fields.title: How was origin of the biological sample altered?
fields.description: Describe each natural or engineered genetic alteration that could affect glycan composition or glycosylation. Add a separate entry for every relevant modification present in the sample. Alterations that are not already represented by the selected organism, strain, or cell line identifier.(Trans effect)

fields.label: Allele
fields.description: Provide the allele designation or textual description of the genetic alteration. Use the nomenclature commonly employed in your organism model or publication.

fields.label: Genomic Alteration Type
fields.description: Describes the type of DNA sequence change affecting the gene or protein. This field captures the structural nature of the variant, such as a substitution, insertion, deletion, or frameshift, independent of how it was generated or its biological effect. Use 'Unknown' if the exact sequence alteration has not been reported.

options.label: Single Nucleotide Variant
options.description: SNVs are single nucleotide positions in genomic DNA at which different sequence alternatives exist.

options.label: Insertion
options.description: The sequence of one or more nucleotides added between two adjacent nucleotides in the sequence.

options.label: Deletion
options.description: The point at which one or more contiguous nucleotides were excised.

options.label: Duplication
options.description: An insertion which derives from, or is identical in sequence to, nucleotides present at a known location in the genome.

options.label: Copy Number Change
options.description: A sequence variant where copies of a feature (CNV) are either increased or decreased.

options.label: Rearrangement
options.description: An alteration of the genome that leads to a change in the structure of one or more chromosomes.

options.label: Gene Fusion
options.description: A sequence variant whereby a two genes have become joined.

options.label: Unknown
options.description: A genomic alteration is known or suspected but the alteration type is not reported.

fields.label: Functional Effect on Gene Product
fields.description: Describes the biological effect of the genetic alteration on the activity of the encoded gene product. This field captures whether the alteration causes a loss, partial loss, gain, or acquisition of a new function, independent of the underlying genetic change. Use 'No Functional Effect Detected' when no measurable functional change has been reported, or 'Function Unknown' when the effect has not been determined.

options.label: Loss of Function (amorph)
options.description: The gene product has substantially reduced or absent normal activity.

options.label: Partial Loss of Function (hypomorph)
options.description: The gene product retains some normal activity but functions below wild-type levels.

options.label: Gain of Function (hypermorph)
options.description: The gene product exhibits increased activity relative to the wild type.

options.label: Novel Function (neomorph)
options.description: The gene product acquires a new activity or biological function not present in the wild type.

options.label: Dominant Negative Effect (antimorph)
options.description: The altered gene product interferes with the function of the normal gene product.

options.label: No Functional Effect Detected (wild-type)
options.description: No measurable change in function has been observed.

options.label: Function Unknown
options.description: The functional consequence has not been determined or reported.

fields.label: Gene
fields.description: Enter the name of the gene affected by the alteration. Use the standard gene symbol recognized for the organism being studied.

fields.label: Species
fields.description: For knock-in experiments involving a gene from another organism, specify the source species of the inserted gene. Select the organism using an NCBI Taxonomy term.

fields.label: Technique
fields.description: Specify the method used to generate the genetic alteration. Include all relevant techniques if multiple approaches contributed to the final genotype.

options.label: Natural Variation
options.description: The alteration occurred naturally and was not intentionally introduced by investigators.

options.label: Targeted Genome Engineering
options.description: The alteration was intentionally introduced using targeted genome editing or engineering methods.

options.label: Gene Transfer
options.description: Genetic material was introduced into cells or organisms using a delivery method such as transfection or transduction.

options.label: Random Mutagenesis
options.description: The alteration was generated through non-targeted mutagenesis methods.

options.label: Gene Expression Modulation
options.description: Gene expression was experimentally increased or decreased without necessarily modifying the genomic sequence.

options.label: Genetic Recombination or Breeding
options.description: The alteration was introduced or combined through sexual reproduction, genetic crosses, or recombination-based approaches.

options.label: Unknown
options.description: The method used to generate or identify the alteration is not known or not reported.

fields.label: Phenotype
fields.description: Describes an observable phenotype associated with the genetic alteration, protein mutation, or biological background. Phenotypes may be morphological, developmental, physiological, behavioral, cellular, molecular, or disease-related.

fields.label: Analyzed Protein Mutation
fields.title: How was the analyzed protein altered?
fields.description: Describe each amino acid change, deletion, insertion, or engineered modification present in the analyzed protein. Add a separate entry for each protein alteration that may affect protein function, glycosylation, or glycan occupancy. (Cis effect)

fields.label: Allele
fields.description: Provide the allele or construct designation associated with the protein variant, if one exists. Use the terminology reported in publications, strain records, plasmid documentation, or laboratory notebooks.

fields.label: Genomic Alteration Type
fields.description: Describes the type of DNA sequence change affecting the gene or protein. This field captures the structural nature of the variant, such as a substitution, insertion, deletion, or frameshift, independent of how it was generated or its biological effect. Use 'Unknown' if the exact sequence alteration has not been reported.

options.label: Single Nucleotide Variant
options.description: SNVs are single nucleotide positions in genomic DNA at which different sequence alternatives exist.

options.label: Insertion
options.description: The sequence of one or more nucleotides added between two adjacent nucleotides in the sequence.

options.label: Deletion
options.description: The point at which one or more contiguous nucleotides were excised.

options.label: Duplication
options.description: An insertion which derives from, or is identical in sequence to, nucleotides present at a known location in the genome.

options.label: Copy Number Change
options.description: A sequence variant where copies of a feature (CNV) are either increased or decreased.

options.label: Rearrangement
options.description: An alteration of the genome that leads to a change in the structure of one or more chromosomes.

options.label: Gene Fusion
options.description: A sequence variant whereby a two genes have become joined.

options.label: Unknown
options.description: A genomic alteration is known or suspected but the alteration type is not reported.

fields.label: Functional Effect on Gene Product
fields.description: Describes the biological effect of the genetic alteration on the activity of the encoded gene product. This field captures whether the alteration causes a loss, partial loss, gain, or acquisition of a new function, independent of the underlying genetic change. Use 'No Functional Effect Detected' when no measurable functional change has been reported, or 'Function Unknown' when the effect has not been determined.

options.label: Loss of Function (amorph)
options.description: The gene product has substantially reduced or absent normal activity.

options.label: Partial Loss of Function (hypomorph)
options.description: The gene product retains some normal activity but functions below wild-type levels.

options.label: Gain of Function (hypermorph)
options.description: The gene product exhibits increased activity relative to the wild type.

options.label: Novel Function (neomorph)
options.description: The gene product acquires a new activity or biological function not present in the wild type.

options.label: Dominant Negative Effect (antimorph)
options.description: The altered gene product interferes with the function of the normal gene product.

options.label: No Functional Effect Detected (wild-type)
options.description: No measurable change in function has been observed.

options.label: Function Unknown
options.description: The functional consequence has not been determined or reported.

general.label: Comment
general.description: Add any additional information that may help others understand, interpret, or reproduce the experiment. Use this field for details that are not captured elsewhere in the submission form.

general.label: Contributor
general.description: List the people and software tools that contributed to generating, processing, analyzing, or curating the dataset. Include all major contributors and assign the role that best describes their involvement.

general.label: Experimental Technique
general.description: Select all experimental techniques used to generate the reported data. Include both acquisition and analytical methods when multiple techniques were part of the workflow.

options.label: MS
options.description: A spectroscopy in which the sample is converted into 'gaseous ions [...] which are then characterized by their mass-to-charge ratios and relative abundances'.

options.label: MS/MS
options.description: A mass spectrometry involving multiple mass-selection steps, with some form of fragmentation occurring between each stage.

options.label: LC-MS
options.description: A mass spectrometry in which a sample mixture is first separated by liquid chromatography.

options.label: LC-MS/MS
options.description: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by liquid chromatography before being ionised and characterised by mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance using two mass spectrometers in series.

options.label: CE-MS
options.description: Any method where the sample is first separated by capillary electrophoresis, before being analysed by mass spectrometry.

options.label: GC-MS
options.description: A mass spectrometry in which a sample mixture is first separated by gas chromatography.

options.label: Imaging MS
options.description: The collection of spatially resolved mass spectra of a sample during microscopy where a pulse laser is used to produce both ionisation and vapourisation and the sample is held in a matrix (such as dihydrobenzoic acid) to protect it from direct laser illumination and to separate the sample molecules. The spectra are used to visualise the spatial distribution of (typically) biomolecules by their molecular masses.

options.label: IMS-MS
options.description: Spectrometry where the ionic species associated with the peaks in an ion mobility spectrum are identified by a mass spectrometer.

options.label: CE
options.description: An electrophoresis that takes place in a capillary.

options.label: HPLC
options.description: A liquid-solid chromatography in which the stationary phase consists of very small particles and the inlet pressure is relatively high.

options.label: IMS
options.description: Spectroscopy where the velocity of gas phase ions in an electric field is measured.

options.label: GC
options.description: A column chromatography 'in which the mobile phase is a gas.'

options.label: Gel Electrophoresis
options.description: A separation method where colloidal particles move at different speeds according to their electrophoretic mobilities in a separation medium consisting of gel, across which an electric field is applied.

options.label: 1D NMR
options.description: Spectroscopy where the energy states of spin-active nuclei placed in a static magnetic field are interrogated by inducing transitions between the states via radio frequency irradiation. Each experiment consists of a sequence of radio frequency pulses with delay periods in between them, and the spectrum is obtained by plotting chemical shift vs. frequency.

options.label: 2D NMR
options.description: A pulsed nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy in which a second frequency dimension is employed to disperse the signals and reveal correlations between interacting nuclei.

options.label: 1H NMR
options.description: Spectroscopy where the energy states of 1H nuclei placed in a static magnetic field are interrogated by inducing transitions between the states via radio frequency irradiation. Each experiment consists of a sequence of radio frequency pulses with delay periods in between them.

options.label: TOCSY
options.description: A pulsed nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that reveals correlations between all nuclei of a spin-system.

options.label: NOESY
options.description: A pulsed 'nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy based on the nuclear Overhauser [enhancement] effect' in which correlations are seen between nuclei that are spatially proximate within a molecule (6 \AA apart).

options.label: Solid-state NMR
options.description: A pulsed nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy in which the response of nuclei with non-zero spin, in a solid sample, to a perturbing magnetic field is detected.

options.label: X-ray Crystallography
options.description: A method for determining structure by directing a beam of X-rays at a single crystal sample and detecting the positions and intensities of the diffracted X-rays as a pattern of spots on a photographic plate. Single crystal X-ray diffraction is used for protein crystallography.

options.label: Cryo-EM
options.description: Microscopy where the specimen, which is cooled in liquid ethane to 180°C, is bombarded with a finely focused (<10 nm diameter) electron beam with an acceleration voltage 50-150 kV under vacuum and the interaction of the electrons with the specimen produces transmitted, secondary, backscattered and diffracted electrons and characteristic X-rays which are detected.

general.label: Publication
general.description: Provide the PubMed ID (PMID) or DOI of the publication describing this dataset. Use the primary publication associated with the reported experiment whenever available.
